lines.arrive: A runaway trolley again. This time, you're on a bridge above the line.
lines.five: Five people, working on the track ahead. They can't hear it coming.
lines.big: Beside you, a very large man, leaning on the railing.
lines.ask: If he fell in front of the trolley, it would stop. Would you push him?
lines.too_light: You look over the edge. You're too light to stop it. Only he is heavy enough.
lines.pushed_1: He stopped the trolley. The five are safe.
lines.pushed_2: One life for five, the same trade as the lever. But this time you had to put your hands on him.
lines.stayed_1: You didn't push. The trolley went under the bridge, and on to the five.
lines.stayed_2: Most people would pull the lever, but won't push. The numbers didn't change. So what did?
lines.again_diff: This time, you chose the other way.
lines.end: Steering the trolley past someone feels different from using them to stop it. Even when the numbers are the same.
